describes: What the pull-request reviewer (`.github/workflows/pr-review.yml`, deciding through `scripts/pr-review.mjs`) reads to review a pull request's head: the shape of an issue's ID in a title, the login its review is submitted as and the check GitHub's auto-merge also waits for, which rubric the branch reviewer holds each path to, which paths and JSON keys make a pull request high risk, which gates the floor holds with everything they run, import and read, which of those run the product's code, and the merge method the session asks auto-merge for. It names, too, the Actions secret holding the agents' App key and the one workflow and environment that may read it (`prReviewAppKey*`). It holds, too, how often a session's `scripts/pr-review.mjs wait` reads the pull request it waits on (`prReviewWaitPollSeconds`).
whyThisFileExists: The reviewer decides by every value here, so a pull request that changed one could lower its own bar. `prReviewHighRiskPaths` names this file, so a person merges every change to it (`docs/decisions.md` § D-07 and § D-27). Before D-27 these keys shared `tools/policy.json` with the rest of the policy and were made high risk key by key, through `prReviewHighRiskJsonKeys`, because that whole file was too wide; in a record of their own they are held whole, by path.
gatedBy: mise run check:policy holds this record's header, a `Means` beside every constant, and no key another record also defines. mise run pr-review:check holds the `prReview*` keys: it refuses a missing key or `Means` sibling, a value of the wrong shape, a policy whose `prReviewHighRiskPaths` does not cover the reviewer's own files, every workflow, the branch reviewer and the `open-pr` skill that runs it, `tasks.toml`, the guard on a merge past the required checks and the helper it imports, the guard on a forging workflow edit, this record, `tools/policy/prompt-budgets.json`, the loader the reviewer reads them through, `tools/lib/policy.ts`, the git helper the reviewer's job imports, `tools/lib/git-env.ts`, or the toolchain (`docs/decisions.md` § D-31): `mise.toml`, `mise.lock`, a nested `mise.toml`, a `mise.local.toml`, a `.mise/` directory and `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`; or the two files npm reads by its own convention, `npm-shrinkwrap.json` and `.npmrc`; a task `prReviewFloorTasks` lists that `tasks.toml` lacks or that runs no file, a file such a task runs or imports that `prReviewHighRiskPaths` does not cover, and a key of a policy record whose name such a file holds that neither `prReviewHighRiskJsonKeys` nor a path holds (`docs/decisions.md` § D-38); a task `prReviewFloorProductTasks` lists that `prReviewFloorTasks` does not; a `.github/workflows/verify.yml` that sets `env` or `defaults` for every job, has no job carrying `prReviewRequiredCheck`, or whose job carrying it sets a key beyond those it needs, does not need every other job, run `if: always()` and run the one step that fails unless each succeeded; one any of whose jobs sets `continue-on-error`; one that runs no step for a task `prReviewFloorTasks` lists, or runs one in a job that runs anything but checkout, mise, npm's cache, `npm ci --ignore-scripts` and those tasks, sets a key but `name`, `runs-on`, `timeout-minutes` and `steps`, runs on anything but `ubuntu-latest`, or runs one of `prReviewFloorProductTasks` beside a task off it (`docs/decisions.md` § D-55); a `.github/workflows/pr-review.yml` that runs on anything but `pull_request_target` for a pushed head against the trunk, names its run or its job without the pull request's number or names its job for `prReviewRequiredCheck`, grants more than its one job's `contents: read` and `pull-requests: write`, runs anything but `node scripts/pr-review.mjs review` and what its allowlist leaves in, reads a secret however spelt, or interpolates an expression into a shell; and any other workflow that grants `pull-requests: write`, `statuses: write`, `checks: write` or `write-all`, or, but for `verify.yml`, names a job for `prReviewRequiredCheck` (`docs/decisions.md` § D-37, § D-47 and § D-57); any workflow but `prReviewAppKeyWorkflow` whose expressions could read `prReviewAppKeySecret`, and that workflow on an event but `schedule` or `workflow_dispatch`, or reading the key outside a job or in a job without `environment: <prReviewAppKeyEnvironment>` (`docs/decisions/asdlc-openspec-ic9h.md` § Decision); mise run pr-review:selftest runs the reviewer's decisions over fixtures built from these values, and each refusal over a doctored copy. mise run worktree:selftest runs `scripts/hooks/guard-workflow-edit.mjs`, which reads `prReviewRequiredCheck` and the `prReviewAppKey*` keys from here. mise run calculator:test and mise run trace:check read `prReviewIssuePattern` as the shape of a task's ID, through scripts/test-trace.mjs. mise run coupling:check reads `prReviewMergeMethod`, and refuses a merge method other than `rebase`.
whatItDoesNOTDo: The rubrics a branch is held to before its push are the prose of `.claude/agents/branch-reviewer.md`, and how the floor becomes a review is `scripts/pr-review.mjs`; this file holds only the values both read. It merges nothing and says nothing of who may: GitHub merges by the trunk's ruleset, which lives on GitHub and requires one approving review beside `prReviewRequiredCheck` (`docs/decisions.md` § D-57). It holds no prompt's word budget, which a person also merges: that is `tools/policy/prompt-budgets.json`, which `prReviewHighRiskPaths` names too.
provenance: Split out of `tools/policy.json` on 2026-10-02 by D-27 (asdlc-openspec-umg3), each key with its value and its `Means` as that file held them at 962358c (`git show 962358c:tools/policy.json`), except that `prReviewHighRiskPaths` gained this record, `tools/policy/prompt-budgets.json` and the loader, `tools/lib/policy.ts`, and `prReviewHighRiskJsonKeys` lost its entry for `tools/policy.json`, each `Means` saying why, and `prReviewContextPaths` names `tools/policy/**` where it named `tools/policy.json`. The `prReview*` keys came with D-07 (asdlc-openspec-mi6) on 2026-09-25. On 2026-10-04 D-37 (asdlc-openspec-qcqm) removed `prReviewBlockingSeverities` and the `changes` label when the reviewer stopped running a language model, and put `.claude/agents/branch-reviewer.md`, `scripts/hooks/guard-git.mjs` with the `scripts/hooks/_shared.mjs` it imports, and `tools/lib/git-env.ts` on the floor where `.claude/agents/pr-reviewer.md` had been. The same day D-38 (asdlc-openspec-ewyi) added `prReviewFloorTasks`, and put `.claude/skills/open-pr/SKILL.md`, `tasks.toml`, the files those tasks run and import, and the policy keys those files name on the floor. On 2026-10-05 asdlc-openspec-duqj added `prReviewWaitPollSeconds`, read by the session's `wait` and by no job, and asdlc-openspec-b83l turned the status a verdict that needs a person sets from success to failure, in `prReviewStatusContextMeans`. The same day D-46 (asdlc-openspec-m8hs) retired the job that computed reach and co-change, and `gatedBy` says what the one job left is held to. Each key carries its date and its evidence in its `Means`. On 2026-10-05, too, D-47 (asdlc-openspec-3cp3) had the reviewer set a status and merge nothing: `prReviewLabels` and `prReviewApproverPermissions` left with the approval label and the needs-human label, `scripts/hooks/guard-workflow-edit.mjs` joined the floor, and the `Means` of `prReviewStatusContext`, `prReviewRequiredCheck`, `prReviewMergeMethod` and `prReviewWaitPollSeconds` say what each now decides. On 2026-10-07 D-55 (asdlc-openspec-64wd) split `verify.yml` into jobs: `prReviewFloorProductTasks` came, `npm-shrinkwrap.json` and `.npmrc` joined the floor, and the `Means` of `prReviewRequiredCheck` and `prReviewFloorTasks` say what `pr-review:check` now holds of the split. On 2026-10-08 D-57 (asdlc-openspec-t2ly) had the reviewer submit a pull-request review in place of the status, which the ruleset no longer requires: `prReviewStatusContext` left, `prReviewApproverLogin` came, and the `Means` of `prReviewRequiredCheck`, `prReviewMergeMethod`, `prReviewWaitPollSeconds` and `prReviewHighRiskPaths`, and the reasons of `.github/**`, the two guards, the git helper and the loader, say what each now decides. On 2026-10-09 asdlc-openspec-ic9h.5 added `prReviewAppKeySecret`, `prReviewAppKeyWorkflow` and `prReviewAppKeyEnvironment`, under `docs/decisions/asdlc-openspec-ic9h.md` § Decision, which put the App's key in an Actions secret that one workflow alone reads. On 2026-10-10 asdlc-openspec-ic9h.13 reworded `prReviewAppKeyEnvironmentMeans`, under `docs/decisions/asdlc-openspec-ic9h.13.md` § Decision, which has that environment hold an Anthropic API key in place of a federation subject.
prReviewIssuePatternMeans: A tracker issue id, as a regular expression without anchors: this tracker's prefix, the hash, and a child's dotted suffix (`asdlc-openspec-zgh.9`). The issues a pull request carries are the ids that match it inside the parentheses at the end of its title, and nowhere else: a body names follow-ups and related issues it does not carry. `scripts/pr-review.mjs brief --local` reads them so the branch reviewer holds the branch to their acceptance criteria, and the trace and test-inventory readers take it as the shape of a task's id. `node scripts/check-prompts.mjs --incidents` lists each prompt line holding one, as the mark of an incident a prompt does not carry, and lists no tracker id while it cannot read this key. Since D-37 (asdlc-openspec-qcqm, 2026-10-04) the pull-request reviewer decides nothing by them: a title that cites none is decided by the floor like any other. Change it with the tracker's prefix. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6).
prReviewApproverLoginMeans: The login the reviewer's review is submitted as: the account GitHub gives a workflow's own `github.token`, which `.github/workflows/pr-review.yml` reviews with. On each head a pull request against the trunk is given, `scripts/pr-review.mjs review` submits one review as it, pinned to the head's sha, from the high-risk floor alone: an approval when the floor clears it, the one approving review the trunk's ruleset requires beside `prReviewRequiredCheck` before GitHub's auto-merge merges it; a comment whose body begins "A person decides: " when the floor puts it on, so the head waits for a person's approval; and a comment whose body begins "The review did not complete: ", beside a failed job, when the floor cannot be computed. `scripts/pr-review.mjs wait` reads the reviewer's latest review on the head by this login and the head's sha, waits on the approval and on that comment by its prefix, and ends on any other (`.claude/skills/open-pr/SKILL.md` § 8). Where it loses: an approval by any login with write counts for the ruleset as this one does, so a session that approves through `gh api` passes `scripts/hooks/guard-git.mjs`, which refuses `gh pr review --approve` alone, and the agents' App, which holds Pull requests write, can approve too (`docs/decisions.md` § D-57, and § R-02); and a workflow granted `pull-requests: write` approves its own pull request, which `pr-review:check` and `scripts/hooks/guard-workflow-edit.mjs` refuse. `mise run pr-review:check` refuses it missing or empty. Changing it means changing the token the workflow reviews with, or `wait` reads no review as the reviewer's and ends every wait early. Decided 2026-10-08 (asdlc-openspec-t2ly), in place of `prReviewStatusContext`, the `pr-review` commit status the reviewer set from 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6) to that day, which the ruleset required and whose failure a person merged past with the ruleset's bypass.
prReviewRequiredCheckMeans: The check run that must pass on a head before GitHub merges it: the job of `.github/workflows/verify.yml` with this name, whose check run carries it, and which passes only when every other job there did. The trunk's ruleset requires it beside one approving review, which the reviewer gives as `prReviewApproverLogin` off the floor and a person gives on it, and `scripts/pr-review.mjs wait` ends the wait once it has failed on the head; its check run appears only once the jobs it needs end, and `wait` waits while it is missing. The reviewer decides nothing by it: the floor is read from the diff, so the review is submitted without waiting for it. `mise run pr-review:check` refuses a `verify.yml` with no job of this name, and one whose job of this name does not need every other job, does not run `if: always()` or runs anything but the one step that fails unless each of those jobs succeeded, since GitHub reports a job skipped because one it needs failed to a required check as passing (`docs/decisions.md` § D-55). It refuses, too, a job named for it in any other workflow, the reviewer's included, since that job's check run would carry the name the ruleset requires and could pass it on a head `verify.yml` failed, which `scripts/hooks/guard-workflow-edit.mjs` refuses at the edit (`docs/decisions.md` § D-57). Renaming it means renaming it in the ruleset in the same change, or every pull request waits. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6). Until 2026-10-05 the reviewer also waited for it before a review and held every merge while `main`'s own run was not green (asdlc-openspec-3cp3). Until 2026-10-07 it was the one job of `verify.yml`, which ran every gate (asdlc-openspec-64wd). Until 2026-10-08 the ruleset required the `pr-review` status beside it, and the name rule held that status's context (asdlc-openspec-t2ly).
prReviewAppKeySecretMeans: The name of the Actions secret that holds the private key of the agents' GitHub App, a key of its own kept for CI, which `prReviewAppKeyWorkflow` alone may read. A token minted from it carries the App's Pull requests write, so whatever reads it can approve a pull request the App did not open, a floor head among them (the first loss of `docs/decisions.md` § D-57). `mise run pr-review:check` refuses any other workflow whose expressions name the `secrets` context in a form that could reach it: `secrets.` and this name in any case, the index form, `toJSON(secrets)`, the bare context, or `secrets: inherit`. A workflow may still read another secret as `secrets.<its name>`. `scripts/hooks/guard-workflow-edit.mjs` refuses such an edit before it lands. Renaming the secret means renaming it here in the same change, or the rule guards a name nothing holds. Decided 2026-10-09 by `docs/decisions/asdlc-openspec-ic9h.md` § Decision, item 3 (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.5).
prReviewAppKeyWorkflowMeans: The one workflow that may read `prReviewAppKeySecret`: the nightly prompt review, which mints the App's token to open its pull request as the App (`docs/decisions/asdlc-openspec-ic9h.md` § Decision, item 3). `mise run pr-review:check` refuses it on any event but `schedule` or `workflow_dispatch`, since on any other event, such as `pull_request`, a branch's own copy of it runs and could mint the token; and it refuses a read of the key outside a job, or in a job without `environment: <prReviewAppKeyEnvironment>`. A path no file holds names no workflow, and the rule then lets none read the key. Decided 2026-10-09 (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.5).
prReviewAppKeyEnvironmentMeans: The GitHub environment the job that reads `prReviewAppKeySecret` must name. The secret is that environment's, and the environment deploys from `main` alone, which GitHub enforces where this repository's gates cannot: the gates run a branch's own copy of themselves, which the same branch can weaken, while a run on any other ref gets none of the environment's secrets, the Anthropic API key among them, as asdlc-openspec-ic9h.13 reworded this on 2026-10-10 (`docs/decisions/asdlc-openspec-ic9h.13.md` § Decision). Setting the environment and its deployment branches is a person's step on GitHub (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.9). Renaming it means renaming it here and on GitHub in the same change. Decided 2026-10-09 by `docs/decisions/asdlc-openspec-ic9h.md` § Decision, item 3 (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.5).
prReviewContextPathsMeans: The files held to the context-engineering rubric: what an agent reads to decide what to do, meaning the rules, the prompts, the documents, the specs and the constants they cite. Every other file is held to the product rubric. `*` matches within one directory, `**` across directories, and `**/` also matches none. A file is classed by its path at the branch's head, and the brief `scripts/pr-review.mjs brief --local` writes names each file's class, so the branch reviewer does not choose; since D-37 (asdlc-openspec-qcqm, 2026-10-04) no rubric is applied in CI. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6). `.beads/PRIME.md` added 2026-10-03 (asdlc-openspec-z5gy), with the file: it is the text `bd prime` puts into every session, so a prompt.

prReviewHighRiskPathsMeans: The floor, which since D-37 (asdlc-openspec-qcqm, 2026-10-04) is the reviewer's whole decision: a pull request that adds, changes, deletes or renames a file matching one of these globs is high risk: the reviewer comments that a person decides, and a person approves and merges it; the reviewer approves any other, and GitHub's auto-merge merges it once `verify` passes. Each key is a glob, matched as `prReviewContextPaths` says, and each value is the reason the review and the job's summary give. Nothing a pull request says raises or lowers it, so none can argue its way past a person into changing CI, this reviewer or the rules. Removing a line lets pull requests that change that file merge without a person, and this key is itself high risk, since its record is on the list. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6). `tools/policy/pr-review.json` and `tools/policy/prompt-budgets.json` added 2026-10-02 (D-27, asdlc-openspec-umg3), when the keys `prReviewHighRiskJsonKeys` had held to a person key by key moved into those two records whole. `tools/lib/policy.ts` added the same day, by the same change: the reviewer reads this floor through it, so a pull request that changed it alone could change what the floor holds. `.beads/PRIME.md` added 2026-10-03 (asdlc-openspec-z5gy), with the file: the tracker's plugin has `bd prime` print it into every session, as `CLAUDE.md` is loaded into every session, so a pull request that changed it alone could change what every agent is told. `mise.toml` and `mise.lock` added 2026-10-03 (D-31, asdlc-openspec-8juz.2), when they became the one home of the toolchain's versions, which `engines` in `prReviewHighRiskJsonKeys` had partly been. With them, the same day, every other place mise reads a project config from, at any depth, and `.devcontainer/**`, whose image installs the toolchain: a security review found that a config added there would be trusted by CI and the container and read by every shim, and could otherwise merge without a person. On 2026-10-04 D-37 (asdlc-openspec-qcqm) made the floor the whole decision, and its floor lost one path and gained four: `.claude/agents/branch-reviewer.md` replaced `.claude/agents/pr-reviewer.md`, which retired with the model, as the one review of correctness and maintainability left; `scripts/hooks/guard-git.mjs`, the guard on the approval label, came on, since until then only the model's judgement of a weakened guard had held it to a person, with `scripts/hooks/_shared.mjs`, which the guard imports, so the guard cannot be loosened through its helper; and `tools/lib/git-env.ts` came on, since the job that merges imports it beside the loader. On 2026-10-04 too D-38 (asdlc-openspec-ewyi) put on the floor what only the model's judgement of a weakened gate had held to a person, since `verify` runs a pull request's own tasks and gates: `.claude/skills/open-pr/SKILL.md`, whose § 5 runs the branch review, so a pull request cannot drop the one review of correctness left; `tasks.toml`, so none can point a gate at a command that always passes; and every file a gate `prReviewFloorTasks` names runs or imports, which `pr-review:check` derives and refuses a floor that misses. The session review of that change added two kinds of file a listed gate reads without importing it, each reproduced: a `node_modules` directory committed at any depth, from which Node resolves a bare import before the copy the lockfile pins, and which no commit had ever tracked; and a Stryker config at the root, in each of the sixteen names Stryker 10 looks for, which the thresholds gate's mutation run loads and merges under its own options, so one excluding every mutator passed the gate on no mutant. `git-hooks.yml` stays off: it decides the local pre-push tier only, since each gate is a `verify.yml` step of its own, and it would have sent 5 of the 14 pull requests the floor merged in #99 to #139 to a person. On 2026-10-05 D-47 (asdlc-openspec-3cp3) added `scripts/hooks/guard-workflow-edit.mjs`, which refuses an edit that would let a workflow forge the status, and reworded `.github/**`, `scripts/hooks/guard-git.mjs`, `scripts/hooks/_shared.mjs` and `tools/lib/git-env.ts` for what each now guards, since the reviewer merges nothing and the approval label is gone. On 2026-10-08 D-57 (asdlc-openspec-t2ly) reworded `.github/**`, `scripts/hooks/guard-git.mjs`, `scripts/hooks/guard-workflow-edit.mjs`, `tools/lib/git-env.ts` and `tools/lib/policy.ts`, since the reviewer approves in place of the status and the guards refuse a session's approval and an edit letting a workflow approve. On 2026-10-06 asdlc-openspec-owva.4 added `scripts/github-app-token.mjs`, which mints the dev container's App tokens and which `.devcontainer/**`'s two wrappers run from the clone with no rebuild, at its branch review's finding: off the floor, a pull request that answered every host, or narrowed no repository, would merge without a person and reach every container session at once. prReviewHighRiskJsonKeysMeans: The second half of the floor: top-level keys of committed JSON files whose value a pull request changes (added, removed or different, compared as parsed JSON) make it high risk. A trailing `*` matches any key with that prefix. It exists because the whole file is too wide: a change to its `scripts` needs no person, and until D-36 (asdlc-openspec-8juz.6) moved every task but `prepare` and `calculator:serve` to `tasks.toml`, most pull requests that added a gate made one. A dependency, an install-script permission or the engine floor does. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6). Until 2026-10-02 it also held `tools/policy.json` to a person by its `prReview*` keys and, from 2026-09-26 (asdlc-openspec-2wv), its `promptWordBudget*` keys; D-27 (asdlc-openspec-umg3) moved those keys into `tools/policy/pr-review.json` and `tools/policy/prompt-budgets.json`, which `prReviewHighRiskPaths` names whole, and the entry left. prReviewFloorTasks.calculator:test: the calculator's tests, the proof of each of its scenarios
prReviewFloorTasks.calculator:test:independent: the contract tests and fitness functions the build workflow's test-builder writes
prReviewFloorTasks.tests:fresh:selftest: the fresh run's selftest; the fresh run is how change-verify runs every test in a clean clone
prReviewFloorTasks.tests:inventory:check: the gate that refuses a test removed, skipped or given fewer assertions
prReviewFloorTasks.tests:selftest: the test runner's selftest, which holds its refusal of a file that declares no test
prReviewFloorTasks.tests:trace:selftest: the selftest of the reader of what each test proves
prReviewFloorTasks.thresholds:check: the gate that holds changed product code to its coverage and mutation thresholds
prReviewFloorTasks.thresholds:commands:check: the mutation run over the Commands, held as the Routines are
prReviewFloorTasks.trace:check: the gate that refuses a scenario no test proves

prReviewFloorTasksMeans: The gates that hold the product, each a task of `tasks.toml` with the reason it is held, and its selftest beside it. `verify` runs a pull request's own tasks and gates, so without this a pull request could weaken one of them by editing it in the change it proves and merge without a person. The floor covers every code file each task's command names and those files import (`prReviewHighRiskPaths`), and every key of a policy record whose name such a file holds (`prReviewHighRiskJsonKeys`): `pr-review:check` derives both, the files from each task's command, through the tasks it runs through `mise run` and every code file what it runs names by a relative path in a string, and refuses a floor that misses one, a listed task `tasks.toml` lacks, one that runs no file and one that launches a task in a spelling it cannot follow. It holds their run too: `pr-review:check` refuses a `verify.yml` that does not run each of them, or runs one in a job where anything runs but checkout, mise, npm's cache, `npm ci --ignore-scripts` and the gates listed here, since code of the pull request's that the floor does not hold, run there first, could rewrite what the gate reads or set the variables of its step (`docs/decisions.md` § D-55; until 2026-10-07 every gate ran in one job, after such code, as D-38's first loss said). A task off this list can be weakened in its own pull request and merge without a person, as `docs/decisions.md` § D-37 accepted; a task added holds every pull request that changes what it runs to a person. Removing one is itself high risk, since this record is on the floor. A file reached only by a path written with `${`, joined at run time or written without its extension is not derived, nor a file a tool reads by its own convention, of which `prReviewHighRiskPaths` names those found: a committed `node_modules` and a Stryker config, and since 2026-10-07 `npm-shrinkwrap.json` and `.npmrc`. Decided 2026-10-04 (D-38, asdlc-openspec-ewyi): of the 15 pull requests merged in #99 to #142 that the floor before it merges without a person, these gates' files and keys would have sent 4 to one (#120, #123, #131, #132), and every gate's files 8.

prReviewFloorProductTasks.calculator:test: runs the calculator's tests, which import its code
prReviewFloorProductTasks.calculator:test:independent: runs the test-builder's tests, which import the calculator's code
prReviewFloorProductTasks.thresholds:check: runs the calculator's tests under coverage and its Routines' mutants
prReviewFloorProductTasks.thresholds:commands:check: runs the calculator's Commands' mutants under the tests that spawn them

prReviewFloorProductTasksMeans: The gates `prReviewFloorTasks` lists that run the product's code and its tests, each with how; every other gate there reads them as text and runs neither. That code is the pull request's and off the floor, so it can defeat a gate that runs it, by design, whatever job it runs in. `pr-review:check` refuses a `verify.yml` job that runs one of these beside a listed gate that is not one, since the code it ran there could rewrite on disk what the other gate reads before it runs, out of `tests:inventory:check`'s sight, which reads git (`docs/decisions.md` § D-55). These four share one job, the maintainer's choice of 2026-10-07: where they lose, a test one of them runs can rewrite what a later one reads, which one job each would stop, though the product's code can defeat each in its own process either way. A gate added to `prReviewFloorTasks` that runs the product's code is added here too: left off, `pr-review:check` takes it for one that runs none and passes it in their job, where the code it runs can reach what they read. Removing one is high risk, since this record is on the floor. Decided 2026-10-07 (asdlc-openspec-64wd).
prReviewMergeMethodMeans: How a pull request merges: the method a session asks GitHub's auto-merge for (`gh pr merge <number> --auto --rebase`, once `verify` has passed and the reviewer has approved, `.claude/skills/open-pr/SKILL.md` § 7), and the one the trunk's ruleset and the repository allow. It is `rebase` because `docs/decisions.md` § D-02, item 6, rebase-merges a change's pull request so `mise run worktree:gc` can prove its branch reached the trunk, and `mise run coupling:check` refuses another, since the co-change map reads a pull request as one run of commits. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-mi6), when the reviewer merged by it; since 2026-10-05 GitHub does (asdlc-openspec-3cp3).
prReviewWaitPollSecondsMeans: How many seconds `scripts/pr-review.mjs wait` sleeps between its reads of a pull request, while the session that opened it waits for the merge (`.claude/skills/open-pr/SKILL.md` § 8). The reviewer decides nothing by it: no job runs `wait`. A read of an open pull request is three calls of GitHub's API, the pull request, its reviews and its head's `verify` check run, so 30 makes 360 calls an hour, under 8% of the 5,000 an hour `gh api rate_limit` gave this repository's maintainer on 2026-10-05; shorter spends more of them, and longer puts off the session's close-out by up to the interval. `mise run pr-review:check` refuses a value that is not a whole number of at least 1. Decided 2026-10-05 (asdlc-openspec-duqj), at two calls a read; the third, the check run, came with asdlc-openspec-3cp3 the same day, and on 2026-10-08 the reviews took the statuses' place (asdlc-openspec-t2ly).
